cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is writing a letter to the people of every nation and language who dwell in all the earth. That's a BIG mailing list, friend. And he opens with, “May your prosperity be multiplied.”

cards.question: King Nebuchadnezzar is writing to the whole world. What is he pleased to declare?

answers.text: The signs and wonders the Most High did for him
The great victories his armies have won in battle
The plans for the next golden statue he will build

cards.text: He can't even get to the story without praising first. Then the king says, “How great are His signs, how mighty His wonders!”

cards.question: In his letter, Nebuchadnezzar says the Most High God's kingdom is an eternal kingdom.

cards.text: Then the king says, “I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.” Friend, that's the peace of a Saturday with every bill paid and nothing on the calendar, and THEN comes a dream.

cards.question: King Nebuchadnezzar is at ease in his palace until a dream leaves him ___.

cards.text: So the king issues a decree to bring all the wise men of Babylon before him to interpret it. One bad dream, friend, and this man calls an ALL-HANDS MEETING.

cards.question: The king tells his dream to the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners, and they are able to interpret it for him.

cards.text: But at last, in comes Daniel, chief of the magicians, whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of the king's god. Everybody else already struck out, and here comes the last man through the door.

cards.question: King Nebuchadnezzar tells Daniel he knows no mystery baffles him. Why is the king so sure?

answers.text: The spirit of the holy gods is in him
He has studied every book in Babylon
He is the oldest of all the wise men

cards.text: Then the king tells the dream: a tree in the middle of the land grows so large and strong that its top reaches the sky. Friend, you can see it from the ends of the earth, so that's not a tree, that's a LANDMARK.

cards.question: Under the king's great dream tree, the beasts of the field find ___, and in its branches the birds of the air ___.

cards.text: Then the king sees a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven. Friend, when somebody comes down from heaven in your dream, you are NOT hitting snooze on that one.

cards.question: The watcher from heaven calls out in a loud voice. What does he order done to the great tree?
The watcher orders the great tree's stump and roots to be pulled out of the ground.

cards.text: Then the watcher starts talking about the tree like it's a person: let him be drenched with the dew of heaven and graze with the beasts. Let his mind be changed from a man's to a beast's till seven times pass him by.

cards.question: The holy ones give a reason for their decision about the tree. What is it?

answers.text: So the living know the Most High rules
So the beasts have a place to graze
So the wise men stop their magic arts

cards.text: The king finishes and turns to Daniel: none of my wise men can interpret it, “But you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.” No pressure, friend, no pressure at ALL.
Daniel hears the dream, and for a time he's perplexed and his thoughts alarm him. I bet that's the face of a man who already knows what it means.

cards.question: Daniel stands there alarmed by the dream. What does King Nebuchadnezzar tell him?

answers.text: Don't let the dream alarm you
Hurry up and tell me right now

cards.question: Daniel finally answers King Nebuchadnezzar. He says he wishes the dream applied to the king's ___.

cards.text: Then Daniel walks back through the dream: the tree that reached the sky, the fruit that fed everybody, the birds nesting in its branches. Every detail, one by one, and friend, that is the LONGEST “we need to talk” I have ever heard.

cards.question: Daniel finishes describing the great tree from the dream. Who does he say the tree is?

cards.text: Daniel goes back over the watcher's words, then says it: “This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree that the Most High has issued against my lord the king”. Friend, I get NERVOUS telling a baker their dough needs a little more flour.

cards.question: Daniel says King Nebuchadnezzar will be driven away from ___ and will feed on ___ like an ox.
Daniel says the king will live this way until he acknowledges that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind.

cards.text: But remember, the watcher said to leave the stump with its roots in the ground. Daniel says that stump means something too, and friend, when your whole tree just got chopped, you take ANY good news you can get.

cards.question: Daniel says the stump left in the ground means King Nebuchadnezzar's ___ will be restored to him.

cards.text: Then Daniel gives advice to a king whose dominion reaches the ends of the earth, and friend, I have never been that bold with ANYBODY. Daniel says if the king takes it, perhaps there will be an extension of his prosperity.

cards.question: What advice does Daniel give King Nebuchadnezzar?

answers.text: Turn from sin and show mercy to the oppressed
Stay hidden in the palace until it all passes
Build a great temple to the Most High God

cards.text: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar, and here's how. Twelve months later, he's strolling on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon, looking out over everything.

cards.question: King Nebuchadnezzar looks out over Babylon from his palace roof. What does he say about it?

answers.text: He built it all by his own power
It was all a gift from the Most High
It has grown too big for one king

cards.text: While the words are still in his mouth, a voice comes from heaven with the sentence from the dream. Friend, the man doesn't even get to finish enjoying his own SENTENCE.

cards.question: The voice from heaven tells King Nebuchadnezzar that the ___ has departed from him.
After the voice from heaven speaks, the sentence against King Nebuchadnezzar is put off for another twelve months.

cards.text: He's driven away and eats grass like an ox, until his hair grows like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird. Friend, I know what it's like to go from the counter to the back of the drawer, and nobody comes back from that on their own.

cards.question: At the end of those days, Nebuchadnezzar looks up to heaven. What happens?

answers.text: His sanity is restored to him
Daniel finds him in the field

cards.text: Out comes praise for the Most High, and he says no one “can restrain His hand or say to Him, ‘What have You done?’” Friend, it only took a dream, a voice from heaven and seven times in the field to get him HERE.

cards.question: Once Nebuchadnezzar's sanity returns, his advisers and nobles leave him out in the fields.

cards.text: He's restored to his throne, his honor and splendor come back, and surpassing greatness is added to him. From eating grass like an ox to MORE than he had before, friend, and I came out of a drawer onto a whole planet, so I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar ends his letter praising the King of heaven. What does he say God is able to do?

answers.text: Humble those who walk in pride
Reveal every mystery in a dream

cards.text: Then the king says, “all His works are true and all His ways are just.” Friend, that is a LONG way from that palace roof.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "we need to talk", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question says Daniel wishes the dream applied to the king's enemies. In Daniel 4:19, Daniel wishes the dream on 'those who hate you' and the interpretation on 'your enemies.' The card puts the wrong noun with 'the dream.' Reword it, for example: 'He says he wishes the dream and its interpretation applied to the king's ___.'

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card calls Nebuchadnezzar 'a king whose dominion reaches the ends of the earth.' That detail comes from Daniel 4:22, but the card cites only Daniel 4:27. No earlier card has told the baker this detail. Either cite Daniel 4:22-27 or drop the 4:22 detail.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Reveal every mystery in a dream' can be argued as right. Nebuchadnezzar himself calls God a 'revealer of mysteries' in Daniel 2:47, after a dream. The question asks what Nebuchadnezzar says God is able to do, so a baker who knows that verse could defend this answer. Replace it with something that is clearly not true of God.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
